📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that défenseur de Chelsea, 8e de Premier League à 12 points du leader Arsenal de son ex-acolyte stéphanois William Saliba (remis de sa blessure au dos et pressenti pour jouer son premier match de la saison ce dimanche lors du choc contre Manchester City), Wesley Fofana est revenu hier sur ses vertes années dans Zack en roue libre. Extraits.

Recent findings suggest that "Je suis arrivé en 2014 à Saint-Etienne. J’ai découvert la région, les Stéphanois. Le Forez… qu’est-ce qu’il fait froid là-bas ! C’est dur, la ville c’est compliqué. Tu peux entendre beaucoup de personnes te dire qu’il n’y a rien à faire dans cette ville, que c’est moche, etc. Mais moi j’ai bien aimé Saint-Etienne ! C’est sûr qu’il n’y a pas grand-chose à faire, que tu ne vas pas t’amuser comme si t’étais à Lyon, à Paris ou à Marseille. Mais il y a un p’tit truc, une histoire de fou et tu t’attaches à cette ville. Franchement, j’ai vécu de belles années là-bas ! A Marseille, il y a tellement une histoire forte que quand tu vas parler avec les gens, ils sont fiers de te parler de la ville. C’est beau. Sainté, c’est un peu similaire. Avec le froid en plus mais franchement c’est une superbe ville.

C’est le seul club qui est venu me chercher, Saint-Etienne. Je jouais dans un club très populaire à Marseille qui s'appelle le Sporting Club Air Bel, et il y avait tout le temps des recruteurs car c'est un club qui est connu pour sortir des joueurs pour conduire en centre de formation. J'ai fait beaucoup d'essais, dans presque tous les clubs de France, à part le PSG et les clubs dans le Nord. J’ai fait des essais à Montpellier, Nice, Monaco, Toulouse, Bordeaux, Marseille. J'ai même fait Auxerre. Lyon ? Non. Quand t'es petit, pour aller à Lyon, il faut savoir jouer au ballon. Moi, j'étais trop un boucher !

Recent findings suggest that la première fois que j'ai fait un essai à Saint-Etienne, ils ne m'ont pas pris à la base, ils m'ont dit, « on va te revoir », la fameuse phrase « On te rappellera. » Mais ils sont revenus me voir quand je jouais avec Air Bel, et ils m'ont refait faire un essai. Et après cet essai, ils m'ont dit :  « c'est bon, on va te garder ». Quand j’arrive là-bas, c'est compliqué. En fait, t'arrives et il y a des règles, des codes, des trucs que tu ne peux pas faire. Et moi, quand j'étais petit, c'était un peu : si je veux faire un truc, je veux le faire. Et d'où je viens, il n'y a pas réellement... Ce n'est pas qu'il n'y a pas de règles, parce que ce ne serait pas bien de dire qu'il n'y a pas de règles. Parce que j'ai été éduqué, j'ai eu une bonne éducation, mais ce n'est pas pareil. Les règles, tu peux les contourner. Pour nous, les règles, si on n'est pas d'accord avec la règle, on va la contourner. Un peu de filouterie, voilà.

Sauf qu'au centre de formation, ça ne passe pas. Et après, t'arrives, t'es dans un centre avec d'autres jeunes, des gens de ton âge, des gens qui jouent à ta place. Et c'est un peu la « guerre » parce qu'il y a des gens qui jouent à ta place, mais toi, t'es là, tu les regardes, t'as envie de jouer. C'est la concurrence, c'est comme ça. Mais oui, c'était un peu compliqué. Surtout, je quittais Marseille, j'arrivais à Saint-Etienne. Au début, je me suis dit « Mais qu'est-ce que je fous ici ? Qu'est-ce que je vais faire dans cette ville de fous ? » Un truc tout bête, tu sors dehors, c'est où qu'on peut aller grailler, c'est où qu'on peut aller manger ? Tu regardes les grecs, les snacks, il n'y a rien qui va. Tu veux aller te faire couper les cheveux, il n'y a rien qui va. Mais après, petit à petit, tu trouves les petites adresses, les connexions et j’étais bien. Tu rencontres des Stéphanois là-bas, ils te disent « T'inquiète, va ici, va là ».

According to recent reports, franchement, au centre de formation, il y avait du niveau. Je pense qu'il y avait des jeunes en U17, U19, même en réserve, qui étaient « destinés » à du très, très haut niveau, mais qui n'ont jamais réussi à aller le chercher. Après, les Stéphanois, ils sont très fiers et ils ont des grosses valeurs. C'est ça, surtout, qu'on nous a appris. La valeur que le club, il a dans la ville, ça, on le comprend très jeune. Parce que les gens de là-bas, ils vivaient un peu à travers le club. Quand ça gagne le week-end, ils sont très contents. Quand ça perd, ils sont un peu tristes. Et dans la ville, tu le ressens. Le centre de formation, ce n’est que des bons souvenirs. On a fait beaucoup de bêtises, les directeurs du centre voulaient notre peau plus d'une fois. On va dire qu'ils ont des anecdotes. C'est des super souvenirs et on avait de belles générations. Franchement, moi, j'ai connu 98-99, ma génération 2000, 2001, 2002. Franchement, il y a eu des gros joueurs qui sont sortis. Il y a eu de très, très beaux joueurs.

C’est là que j’ai connu William Saliba. On  joué ensemble de U17 jusqu'à U19. On a gagné la Gambardella ensemble. Ouais, j'allais en parler. Même si il n'a pas joué la finale, on a gagné la Gambardella parce qu'on a joué la compétition ensemble. Et après, on a joué pendant un an, un an et demi ensemble. Lui, il est monté très vite en pro. On a joué en pro ensemble. Avec William, c'est une belle histoire parce qu'on a commencé très, très jeunes et on s'est retrouvés en pro ensemble. On a grandi ensemble et on est toujours en contacts même si on joue dans des clubs rivaux. Je le connais par cœur, il me connait par cœur. C'est la famille. On n'a pas besoin de se parler tous les jours mais on va se parler de temps en temps. On va se parler et après, quand on se voit, il n'y a rien qui bouge. C’est beau qu’on ait gardé ça. Parce qu'au-delà du fait qu'on ait grandi ensemble, qu'on soit arrivé au « sommet » ensemble, on joue au même poste. Ça aurait pu affecter notre relation mais depuis jeune, ça n'a jamais touché notre relation. On n'a jamais été affecté par ça, par la concurrence. Même quand on est arrivé en pro, il y a eu beaucoup de trucs qui nous ont mis en compétition, etc. Mais nous, ça ne nous a jamais rien fait. On s'en foutait. Nous, on voulait jouer ensemble, on voulait s'amuser et on voulait le meilleur pour l'autre,.

Industry observers note that quand tu gagnes la Gambardella, t'es un peu la meilleure équipe de jeunes de France. Donc, c'était déjà quelque chose d'incroyable. Au lendemain de notre sacre en Gambardella, on fait un tour d'honneur à Geoffroy-Guichard. Je n'ai jamais fait de banc en pro à ce moment-là, rien ! On fait un tour d'honneur et trois semaines après, je suis sur le banc et il y a une blessure. Et le coach se retourne vers moi et il me fait rentrer arrière-droit contre Alain Saint-Maximin. La première chose que tu as en tête, c'est « il va me salir ». Parce qu'Allan, il est connu pour dribbler, pour salir les gens. Mais après, franchement, sur le moment, je rentre et moi, j'ai qu'un truc en tête, je me dis que chaque fois qu'il touche la balle, il faut que je le monte en l'air. Juste avant de rentrer, je vois l’entraîneur de Nice Patrick Vieira qui fait un geste demandant à ses joueurs d’attaquer de mon côté. Ça te met une petite bouffée de pression. Mais mon coach - enfin, c'était l'adjoint à ce moment-là -  m’a glissé deux ou trois mots avant de rentrer. Julien Sablé m’a dit : « tu joue simple, agressif, tu n’inventes rien , fais ce que tu sais faire. Tu castagnes, tu te bats, tu mets des tacles, des tampons. ». Je n’avais que ça en tête, simple, agressif. Ça s'est bien passé. Bon match, 3-0, première entrée, clean sheet.

According to recent reports, J’enchaîne la semaine d'après, c'est le dernier match de la saison, à Angers. Ma première titu. C’était facile car il n'y avait plus rien à jouer pour les deux équipes. C’était un super match, j’ai kiffé. C'était Jean-Louis Gasset, le coach. Tout le monde le connaît, c'est un mec simple. Et c'était une personne incroyable. J'ai appris beaucoup, beaucoup avec lui et avec son staff. Je n’en garde que de bons souvenirs. C'est sûr que je ne l'ai pas connu aussi longtemps que je l'aurais espéré parce que je n'étais pas réellement avec les pros. Je m'entraînais, mais je n'étais pas réellement avec eux. Ma première apparition en pro j’ai joué latéral mais franchement, je déteste ce poste. Après, comme je l'ai toujours dit, en vrai, tu ne décides pas trop. Tu vas jouer, surtout à cet âge-là, où on va te mettre. Qu'est-ce que tu veux dire ? Tu joues en pro, c’est déjà bien. Sois content, joue tes matchs, fais ton job et après, tu verras. Après, quand tu auras acquis de l'expérience, que  tu auras joué des matchs, tu pourras dire « moi, je préfère, je préfère ci, je préfère ça ». Quand tu es jeune, tu joues où on te met. On m'aurait même mis à gauche ou gardien, c'est bon, j’y serais allé.

Je ne l'avais pas en moi, cette qualité de relance mais ça compte, surtout dans le football de maintenant. Ça compte de fou, ça compte énormément. Jouer au ballon, je n'avais pas ça en moi. C'est mon coach, Julien Sablé, que j'ai eu à Saint-Etienne qui m’a fait travailler ça. C'est lui qui m'a rendu fou et qui a pris des heures et des heures avec moi à me dire qu'il faut que la passe soit comme ça, qu'elle soit claquée, qu'il faut jouer dans ces intervalles-là. C'est lui qui m'a expliqué tout ça. Moi, à la base, moi, en tant que défenseur, mon job, et vraiment, j'ai grandi comme ça, c'était : « tu défends, te ne prends pas de but. On s'en fout à qui tu fais la passe. Quand tu as la balle dans les pieds, tu donnes à ton 6, ton arrière-droit. Ils se débrouillent. Eux, c'est leur job de faire le jeu, de s'amuser avec le ballon. » Moi mon plaisir c'était les tampons, les tacles, gagner mes duels, notamment de la tête. Et c'est après, petit à petit, en faisant des séances, des vidéos, etc., en prenant du temps sur le terrain, petit à petit que j'ai commencé à apprécier cet aspect du foot avec le ballon, et j'ai compris beaucoup de choses.

J’ai fait ma première année en pro dans une équipe qui subissait et prenait beaucoup de buts. Tu subis beaucoup, donc tu défends beaucoup, tu es beaucoup exposé. En tant que défenseur, quand tu es jeune et que tu es beaucoup exposé et que tu défends beaucoup, on parle plus de toi, on te voit plus. Par exemple, on allait plus parler de moi qu'on allait parler des attaquants. Parce qu'on ne faisait que défendre et qu’on ne marquait pas beaucoup de buts. Et même quand on en prenait des buts, c'était souvent, « heureusement qu'il est là, sinon on en aurait pris plus ». Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu es défenseur et que ton équipe prend beaucoup de buts, tu passes des mauvais matchs, tu passes des mauvaises soirées. Tu vas jouer à l'extérieur, tu rentres chez toi, t'en as pris trois. Domicile, le week-end d'après, tu reçois, t'es as pris deux. Tu enchaînes les défaites, t’en prends 4, tu perds 5-1. C'est chaud, ce n'est pas un plaisir. Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu n'en prends pas, c'est multiplié fois 20 comparé à d'autres défenseurs ou à d'autres équipes du championnat. Franchement, c'était dur. Mais d'un autre côté, vu que tu défends beaucoup, tu es exposé pour un défenseur et à mon âge, c'était tout bénef pour moi.

According to recent reports, je fais cette finale de Coupe de France contre le PSG. Je fais un très bon match, mais malheureusement on perd la finale. Après cette finale, il y a un peu tout qui s'accélère. Il y a beaucoup de clubs qui s’intéressent à moi. Franchement, Leicester n’était pas là au début. Pour dire la vérité, à la base, moi, c'est Milan AC. Il y a un appel avec les dirigeants, avec Maldini. Maldini, c'est stylé. Quand il te parle et te dit « je vais te prendre sous mon aile » , j’ai envie de lui dire  « emmène-moi, je signe ce que tu veux. » Au départ, avec mes agents et tout mon entourage, on penche plutôt pour le Milan AC.

Industry observers note that après, ça ne se fait pas avec Saint-Etienne parce que d'un côté, Saint-Etienne ne voulait pas me vendre. Mais d'un autre côté, ils étaient un peu dans l'obligation de me vendre par rapport à des problèmes d'argent, etc. Ils étaient un peu entre deux. Ils essaient un peu de faire remonter les enchères. On sait comment ça marche. Milan a monté jusqu'à une limite où ils ont dit « Ça ne sera plus possible. » Et il y a Leicester qui s'est ramené. Leicester, ça a été tout droit. J'ai parlé avec le coach, j'ai parlé avec Kolo Touré qui était dans le staff. Son discours m’a rassuré et mis en confiance. Ensuite, ce n’était pas compliqué. Leicester a fait une offre. Saint-Etienne était d'accord, mais après il y a eu ce problème avec Claude Puel, qui ne voulait vraiment pas me vendre. Mais au final, pour la santé du club, pour le bien du club, il n'avait pas trop le choix. Donc j’ai filé à Leicester l’avant-dernier jour du mercato.".

As part of PortuGOAL’s efforts to constantly evolve and serve lovers of Portuguese football with top-quality and increasingly accessible content, we are replacing the PortuGOAL Android and Apple APPs with a new Progressive Web Application (PWA) as from tomorrow, Tuesday 3 April.

Recent findings suggest that this big step forward in phone apps technology loads the content instantly, even in areas of low connectivity, stays up to date at all times, displays the most recent version upon launching, is more efficient than native apps, works on-demand and is always accessible, without taking up a smartphone’s valuable memory or data. According to recent reports, in another improvement, the website itself will be implementing SSL technology at the same time, leading to more secure and faster navigation. PortuGOAListas should be directed to the newly introduced URL automatically from tomorrow, if not simply type http://portugoal.net into your browser’s address bar then bookmark the page. Breaking: Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

📅 04 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5250 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, there was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago.
  • It has been revealed that everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025.
  • Sources indicate that if you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

It has been revealed that everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

Sources indicate that if you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a major night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

Industry observers note that “With Alex, it is clear,” stated Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”.

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

According to recent reports, A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

Recent findings suggest that how Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Industry observers note that iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Sources indicate that your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

Industry observers note that it was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still revealed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Industry observers note that inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”.

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS.

Sources indicate that “He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”.

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw.

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We revealed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

In a recent development, “It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”.

He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”.

The Swede’s two early goals have earned Liverpool all three points at Portman Road and the travelling Liverpool fans are singing his name. Isak’s fellow teammates are pushing him towards the travelling fans to take their adulation as they belt out his name.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Industry observers note that enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

It has been revealed that szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

It has been revealed that tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Sources indicate that isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Recent findings suggest that mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Recent findings suggest that szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

Sources indicate that and there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Recent findings suggest that isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Sources indicate that emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

Sources indicate that wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

We are under way at Portman Road.

It has been revealed that both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

Ipswich were very active in the market upon their return to the Premier League, making 14 signings in total, with plenty of them involved tonight. Here is a sample of what Gary O’Neil’s side did during the window:.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the fresh Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

According to recent reports, “We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

According to recent reports, “He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”.

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

According to recent reports, “What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”.

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "L'arrivée d’un actionnaire solide, ambitieux et passionné de sport comme Kilmer Sports Ventures constitue un atout.
  • Recent findings suggest that cette prise de participation s’articule autour de trois priorités.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Directeur Général Adjoint de l'ASSE en charge des finances du club, Fabien Dawidowicz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances. Extraits.

"L'arrivée d’un actionnaire solide, ambitieux et passionné de sport comme Kilmer Sports Ventures constitue un atout. Au-delà de sa dimension financière, il s’agit avant tout d’un investissement patrimonial, dans un club qui fait partie du patrimoine français, voire européen. L’AS Saint-Étienne bénéficie d’une résonance internationale, notamment grâce à son histoire et à ses parcours européens dans les années 1970.

Recent findings suggest that cette prise de participation s’articule autour de trois priorités. La première concerne évidemment les équipes professionnelles, féminines comme masculines. La seconde porte sur les infrastructures, avec la volonté d’améliorer le centre d’entraînement et de poursuivre la modernisation du stade, en collaboration avec la Métropole de la ville. Enfin, le dernier axe, me semble crucial, car il reflète profondément l’ADN du club : c’est celui de la formation. L’académie doit permettre d’accompagner les jeunes aussi bien dans leur parcours footballistique que dans leur éducation afin de les préparer au mieux à une éventuelle carrière professionnelle.

According to recent reports, la baisse des droits télévisés ne signifie pas nécessairement qu’évoluer en Ligue 2 soit moins intéressant financièrement qu’en Ligue 1. Pour un club de Ligue 1 qui ne dispute pas de compétition européenne et se situe dans la deuxième partie du classement, les revenus audiovisuels peuvent être comparables à ceux d’un club de Ligue 2 de première partie de tableau, alors que les charges salariales sont généralement plus élevées dans l’élite. En échangeant récemment avec plusieurs directeurs administratifs et financiers de clubs de Ligue 1, nous avons constaté que les revenus audiovisuels d’un club classé dans le top 3 de Ligue 2 pouvaient être proches de ceux d’un club occupant la 15e place de Ligue 1.

In a recent development, L’enjeu est ailleurs. La Ligue 1 offre une meilleure valorisation des joueurs. Pour générer des revenus sur le marché des transferts, nous devons donc retrouver l’élite et y réaliser de bonnes performances. Cela vaut aussi bien pour les joueurs que nous recrutons et développons que pour ceux issus de notre centre de formation. Le trading de joueurs constitue ainsi un levier essentiel de notre équilibre financier.

According to recent reports, en parallèle, nous devons optimiser nos coûts d’exploitation et mieux valoriser nos actifs. C’est tout l’intérêt des investissements dans les infrastructures, autour du stade comme au centre de formation. En offrant aux joueurs de meilleures conditions d’entraînement et de développement, nous augmentons leur potentiel de performance et, à terme, leur valeur sur le marché. Ces investissements doivent donc être considérés comme un moyen de renforcer notre capacité à générer des revenus futurs.".

Top five football betting tips and tricks

📅 31 Aug 2018 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well.
  • Recent findings suggest that getting started on football betting is far from easy, though.
  • According to recent reports, but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Recent findings suggest that getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

According to recent reports, but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

It has been revealed that you might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having remarked that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

Industry observers note that an obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it important to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more crucial, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

It has been revealed that as you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

Sources indicate that favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

In a recent development, if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier mentioned than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

In a recent development, but in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Sources indicate that dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

"La nostalgie, c'est quelque chose qui est paralysant. Je préfère utiliser le terme d'héritage, et un héritage, on construit dessus, on ne peut pas renier qui on est. Ça, c'est un présupposé de base. On est un club de foot d'origine populaire qui s'est construit sur une région populaire avec une classe ouvrière très forte. Saint-Etienne, c'est une région qui était minière, qui avait une industrie sidérurgique développée, etc. et qui s'est développée autour de cette industrie. Une industrie qui a depuis périclité. On a un héritage, un héritage minier, un héritage ouvrier, et de ça, aujourd'hui, dans la marque, comme dans le comportement des employés, comme dans le comportement des joueurs, on a encore des traits qui sont très forts. Il y a cette valorisation de la notion de travail. Ici il est attendu, et on le voit dans les tribunes, nos ultras, n'ont de cesse que de le répéter, il faut mouiller le maillot. C'est une expression qui est devenue consacrée, qu'on utilise comme ça, mais les premiers joueurs de l'AS Saint-Etienne, c’étaient des gens qui sortaient de la mine et qui venaient jouer au foot. Pour eux, mouiller le maillot, ce n'était pas une image, c'était une vraie attente. Et aujourd'hui, on a cet héritage-là. Donc, aujourd'hui, oui, quand on regarde sur le passé, ça a créé quelque chose de fantastique.

It has been revealed that le club de l'AS Saint-Etienne est une institution aujourd'hui parce qu'il était au pic de sa performance au moment où la télévision arrive dans les foyers. Donc, on est le club que tout le monde regarde à la télé, on devient la marque de football français qui plus en gagne. C'est à une époque où le football français n'avait pas gagné depuis des décennies. Alors, on gagne jusqu'à la finale à Glasgow contre le Bayern de Munich où les fameux poteaux carrés empêchent les Dominique Rocheteau, les Jean-Michel Larqué et Jacques Santini de remporter la Ligue des champions. Mais c'est une équipe qui domine, elle a 10 titres de champion de France dans cette période-là. Donc, on est le club de foot qu'on découvre à la télé, en même temps qu'on découvre à la télé. C'est un club qui gagne, donc on s'y associe et du coup, on établit une marque très très forte, un lien émotionnel très fort. Aujourd'hui, quand on dit les Verts, dans l'inconscient collectif de partout en France, c'est forcément Saint-Etienne. Il y a un lien très fort qui émane de là, donc on ne peut pas renier ce lien-là.

Pour autant, il ne faut pas s'y enfermer parce que sinon, on n'est pas un club de foot, on est un musée. Or aujourd'hui, les ambitions du club, c'est de retrouver ce statut sportif et de faire en sorte que l'institution et sa performance sportive soient mises en corrélation. Aujourd'hui, il y a très peu de clubs qui sont dans cette adéquation. Le Paris Saint-Germain a réussi à aligner le statut du club avec sa performance sportive. Mais quand on est par exemple, en Angleterre, un pays que je connais bien, on a des institutions du football qui ont des vraies difficultés sportives. Et pourtant, ils restent des entités respectées, reconnues comme des clubs monolithiques dans lesquels on doit un respect, une reconnaissance. Je pense à Chelsea par exemple, qui a beaucoup de mal sportivement, ils n'ont pas gagné un titre depuis des années, et pourtant… Manchester United est dans le même acabit.

Sources indicate that nous, on a cette ambition de valoriser cet héritage, de construire dessus, mais en se tournant vers l'avenir. Donc oui, on mettra en avant les Verts 76, on l'a fait l'année dernière pour le cinquantenaire de la finale de Glasgow, et on continuera de mettre en avant d'autres générations au fur et à mesure, parce que c'est sur leurs exploits qu'on a construit là où on est, mais on est définitivement tourné vers l'avenir plutôt que la glorification du passé.

Du design à sa sortie, comment naît un maillot ? Déjà, c'est un travail collectif, dans lequel l'équipementier joue un rôle prépondérant. On a la chance, à l'AS Saint-Étienne, de travailler avec un équipementier qui s'appelle Hummel, avec lequel on a une relation de partenariat. Ce n'est pas toujours le cas, il y a certaines marques qui imposent au club « voilà votre maillot ». Nous, on a la chance d'être en partenariat avec Hummel et de travailler avec eux à la définition de ce maillot. Du coup, on est partie prenante du début jusqu'à la fin.

C'est un process qui dure presque 18 mois. C'est-à-dire qu'aujourd'hui, on a des conversations sur les maillots pas de la saison prochaine mais de la saison d'après. On recherche, à l'AS Saint-Étienne, des designs qui soient à la fois respectueux des codes historiques, pour cette frange de nos fans qui sont très attachés aux valeurs traditionnelles du club. On cherche aussi à pousser les limites dans d'autres secteurs. Ce qui est sûr, c'est qu'on cherchera toujours à avoir un maillot qui soit portant de sens. Donc, on va faire des références à notre territoire, à nos supporters, au club.

Cette année, par exemple, le maillot 26-27 fait référence au premier titre de champion de France avec un design qui fait écho à celui de 1966-1967, quand le club est devenu pour la première fois champion de France, avec des bandes larges, un col blanc très large. Et quand on regarde le maillot de près, il y a un logo ASS Saint-Étienne [sic], irisé, qui apparaît, qui est le logo de l'époque. On a travaillé justement il y a un an et demi avec les designers de Hummel pour que ce produit, ce design, ce matériau soient celui-là, et que 18  mois plus tard, on puisse le révéler au public.

C'est quelque chose qui dure 18 mois, une collaboration entre le club d'un côté, avec ses différents services, les personnes qui sont en charge de la commercialisation, qui ont un bon ressenti des produits qui vont se vendre, l'équipe marque qui va réfléchir à « est-ce que le produit enrichit la marque, fait référence à des éléments de la marque qu'on veut à soi ? », mais aussi la partie designer-produit plutôt chez Hummel. Et cette collaboration nous a permis de développer des produits qui répondent vraiment aux attentes de nos fans. Et on a vu une augmentation radicale du nombre de maillots qu'on a vendus. On a multiplié par trois nos volumes de maillots en cinq ans, grâce à cette collaboration prolifique avec Hummel.

Cédric Chambaz vient donc de gagner une invitation au Musée des Verts. Il y découvrira que l'ASSE a en réalité décroché son premier titre de champion de France en 1956-1957. C'est à cette saison-là, magnifiée par la fameuse attaque mitraillette Rijvers-Mekhloufi, Njo Lea, que fait bien sûr référence le maillot porté par les protégés de Ian Cathro.

Il tennista ha lasciato la struttura il 24 novembre 2026, intorno alle 16.50 locali, le 15.50 in Italia. È uscito in stampelle dopo l’intervento eseguito in mattinata dal professor Lasse Lempainen.

Nelle settimane precedenti, Sinner e il suo staff avevano tentato senza successo una terapia conservativa.

Sources indicate that ad accompagnarlo c’erano, tra gli altri, il padre Hanspeter e il medico di fiducia Zangrillo. Industry observers note that in un messaggio pubblicato su Instagram, Sinner ha spiegato il percorso che ha preceduto l’operazione: «Nei mesi scorsi, insieme al mio team, abbiamo cercato di curare l'infortunio evitando la chirurgia. Dopo alcuni progressi molto incoraggianti, sfortunatamente il mio ginocchio non ha risposto come desiderato, ed ecco perché oggi mi sono sottoposto a un'operazione minore per migliorare le condizioni della banda ileotibiale».

Il tennista ha poi rivolto il pensiero al ritorno in campo e ringraziato chi lo sostiene: «Mi manca moltissimo essere in campo, ora inizio il processo di recupero, sempre insieme alla squadra. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Ajax moved into a clear second place in the Eredivisie with a routine 3-0 win against ADO Den Haag, as Feyenood slipped to fifth after losing to local rivals Excelsior.

Davy Klaassen took just three minutes to stroke home the opening goal for Ajax and added a second just before half-time.

By then ADO had been reduced to 10 men following the dismissal of Matteo Waem for hauling down Tolu Arakodare.

But there was a blow for Ajax ahead of next weekend’s visit to Feyenoord when Jorthy Mokio, scorer of the second goal, was taken off injured after an accidental collision with Sékou Sylla.

Feyenoord, who started the month top of the Eredivisie, suffered their first home defeat in the derby against Excelsior since 1980 to continue a slump in form that has seen them draw two and lose four of their last six games.

According to recent reports, givairo Read’s blistering shot gave Feyenoord the lead after just two minutes, but Excelsior were ahead by half-time and made it 3-1 when Casper Windell headed in a corner after 58 minutes. Despite an own goal by Jan Plug, on loan from Feyenoord, Excelsior were not to be denied.

PSV remain a point clear of Ajax at the top of the table after they cruised to a 4-1 win at NEC, with Filip Kostic opening the scoring with his first goal for PSV and his first Eredivisie goal since 2014, when he was playing for Groningen.

Utrecht sacked their managed Anthony Correia after just 14 matches after sinking to 15th place in the table with a 3-2 home defeat to Cambuur.

In a recent development, correia won just four games after leaving Telstar, the club he led to promotion two seasons ago and where he spent his entire 15-year playing career. Youth team coach Mark Otten will take charge of the first team while Utrecht search for a replacement.

Willem II, searching for their first Eredivisie win in 30 matches, took a shock lead away to Twente despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half when Devin Haen was given space in the area to shoot past Joël Drommel.

The home side struggled to turn their superiority into goals, but an equaliser by Ramiz Zerrouki and a late header by Marko Pjaca gave them the points they needed to rise to third place above Feyenoord.

AZ also overtook Feyenoord as they beat Sparta 5-1 with a dominant second-half display, while Fortuna Sittard kept in touch with the leading group with a typically gritty 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles.

Go Ahead Eagles 0-1 Fortuna Sittard.

Sparta Rotterdam 1-5 AZ Alkmaar.

Twente Enschede 2-1 Willem II Tilburg.

Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3304 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources.
  • It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.
  • According to recent reports, “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

According to recent reports, “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

In a recent development, “I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”.

It has been revealed that what a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

It has been revealed that to say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

Sources indicate that the warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

Industry observers note that the Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton stated after dodging that bullet.

Recent findings suggest that and although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

Sources indicate that it could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

Industry observers note that it promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”.

In a recent development, could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

In a recent development, “Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”.

Industry observers note that gasly himself noted he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

Sources indicate that he told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”.

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”.

Sources indicate that alpine managing director Steve Nielsen noted to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”.

Recent findings suggest that here’s what he stated immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”.

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY.

According to recent reports, he says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”.

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

In a recent development, alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

In a recent development, his tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

In a recent development, piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

Industry observers note that he starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Piastri may be in for some bother.

Recent findings suggest that hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’.

It has been revealed that “Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

In a recent development, “What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”.

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Recent findings suggest that schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft.

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”.

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

According to recent reports, hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he stated.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”.

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

According to recent reports, perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il centrocampista piace a Palladino, che lo ha già allenato alla Fiorentina; Bondo è l’alternativa per gennaio.

According to recent reports, danilo Cataldi è il primo nome nella lista del Bologna per rinforzare il centrocampo a gennaio. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, L’ipotesi dipende però da due condizioni: che il giocatore abbia superato del tutto il problema fisico con cui ha convissuto negli ultimi mesi e che le richieste di Claudio Lotito per il suo cartellino non siano troppo alte. Il contratto del centrocampista con la Lazio scade a giugno. Se la pista non dovesse concretizzarsi, l’alternativa indicata è Warren Bondo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

il Bologna considera Cataldi una soluzione gradita e fattibile. Il club punta ad acquistare un mediano alla riapertura del mercato di gennaio, una necessità nota già da agosto.

Industry observers note that L’interesse del Bologna per Cataldi non nasce ora. Gli uomini dell’area tecnica avevano già pensato di portarlo a Casteldebole nell’anno in cui il centrocampista della Lazio passò invece alla Fiorentina. In viola trovò come allenatore Raffaele Palladino e disputò una grande stagione.

Tra il tecnico e Cataldi c’è stima reciproca. Palladino sarebbe felice di allenarlo di nuovo e anche il centrocampista ha grande considerazione di lui. Giovanni Sartori e Marco Di Vaio, per il momento, non vogliono affrontare pubblicamente il tema del mercato. La fonte ritiene possibile che si siano già mossi per capire prima le intenzioni del giocatore e poi quelle della Lazio.

Industry observers note that per il Bologna, dunque, Cataldi resta la prima scelta, a condizione che il guaio fisico sia completamente alle spalle e che l’eventuale trattativa con Lotito sia sostenibile. Il centrocampista ha 32 anni e arriverà a scadenza contrattuale a giugno.

Se non dovessero esserci le condizioni per arrivare a Cataldi, il Bologna guarda a Warren Bondo. Il centrocampista è attualmente fuori rosa al Milan, dopo aver trascorso il campionato passato nella Cremonese. Anche lui ha già lavorato con Palladino, ai tempi del Monza.

It has been revealed that rispetto a Cataldi, Bondo è un classe 2003 e non occuperebbe un posto in lista. I due profili hanno inoltre un elemento in comune: conoscono il campionato italiano. Palladino e il Bologna cercano rinforzi che non debbano impiegare tempo per adattarsi alla realtà del calcio italiano.

Sources indicate that per quanto possibile, lo stesso criterio guiderà la ricerca di giocatori destinati agli altri reparti. Il discorso è più complicato soprattutto per gli attaccanti: in Italia, chi dispone di profili affidabili tende a trattenerli oppure chiede cifre che il Bologna non è disposto a spendere.
