Latest Update: Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1275 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • It has been revealed that is football a moral force for good?
  • Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

It has been revealed that is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

According to recent reports, in not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Sources indicate that yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In a recent development, in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

Recent findings suggest that the readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Marathon skater Judith Krabbenborg has taken advantage of the early cold snap to smash the world one-hour record for skating on natural ice.

The 29-year-old took to the ice in Winterswijk, Gelderland, at 8.30am on Tuesday and covered a distance of 34 kilometres 878 metres, beating the previous women’s record by 2.6 kilometres.

“I could feel my legs and my back hurting at the end, but there were so many people standing on the sidelines that it gave me energy,” she told NOS.

The previous record, set four years ago by Femke Mossinkoff, also in Winterswijk, was the first official time for the hour by a woman on natural ice. On the same day Bart Vreugdenhil set the current men’s record of 36 kilometers 717 metres.

Most skating records are set on artificial ice, but Winterswijk is one of three arenas where the local club has been able to create a natural arena for early-morning skaters during the recent cold weather.

The all-time women’s record is 40 kilometres 569 metres, set by another Dutch skater, Carien Kleibeuker, in Inzell, Austria, in 2015.

The rink at Winterswijk closed a few hours after Krabbenborg’s record-breaking skate as the ice started to melt, but it is expected to be available again on Wednesday morning.

Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4379 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was the definition of a hard-earned point.
  • It has been revealed that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
  • Sources indicate that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

It has been revealed that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Sources indicate that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

Recent findings suggest that “It highlights where we have potential,” he remarked. “There are elements to improve offensively.

Recent findings suggest that “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads revealed significant character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a upcoming manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

According to recent reports, when Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

In a recent development, bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another newly introduced signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Industry observers note that justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

Industry observers note that that is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Sources indicate that speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss noted: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

Recent findings suggest that “We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

Recent findings suggest that 3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV.

"Since the latest manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE.

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9.

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

According to recent reports, smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

Sources indicate that the noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Recent findings suggest that amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

Bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

According to recent reports, ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

Sources indicate that murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

It has been revealed that the current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Recent findings suggest that safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

It has been revealed that newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

It has been revealed that the pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

Recent findings suggest that jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

Newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

It has been revealed that newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

According to recent reports, just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

According to recent reports, newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm.

In a recent development, A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF.

Sources indicate that there will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

Sources indicate that it’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Industry observers note that oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

It has been revealed that what a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0.

It has been revealed that st James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Industry observers note that bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Industry observers note that despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. Fresh signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Les sites FLASHSCORE et SOFASCORE ont figé leurs statistiques à l'issue de la rencontre remportée par les Verts à Reims (1-0), pour le compte de la 13me journée de Ligue 2.

Recent findings suggest that sur les vingt données extraites des deux plateformes sportives, les deux équipes ne sont pas parvenues à se départager : dix statistiques sont en faveur des Verts, les dix autres, fatalement, pour le Stade de Reims. Match nul donc.

Dans le jeu avec et sans ballon, les Stéphanois ont perdu le match de la possession (46% vs 54%), tout comme ils l'avaient perdu contre Montpellier (45% vs 55%), à Metz (46% vs 54%), au Red Star (41% vs 59%) et à Sochaux (47% vs 53%). Cinq défaites en ce qui concerne le monopole du ballon mais quatre victoires et un nul au coup de sifflet final (quatre prétendants à la montée rencontrés). Cependant, les Verts ont devancé leur adversaire du soir dans les duels relatifs à la distance kilométrique parcourue (104,3 km vs 98,3 km) et aux sprints à haute intensité (121 vs 115).

Pour ce qui est des passes, les Champenois sont devant partout : les passes réussies (87% vs 83%), les passes longues réussies (52% vs 33%) ainsi que les passes réussies dans le dernier tiers (74% vs 64%). Après Sochaux, Montpellier, Metz et le Red Star, c'est donc la cinquième fois de la saison que les Stéphanois ne dominent pas leur sujet dans ce domaine, en étant même en dessous de leur moyenne constatée avant cette 13ème journée. Cinq défaites dans le match des passes cette fois-ci, pour quatre victoires et un nul à la fin du temps réglementaire.

Sur le plan offensif, Sainté domine Reims sur cinq des huit métriques remontées avec notamment un xG de 1,45 (vs 0,97), un xGOT de 1,06 (vs 0.16), 21 ballons touchés dans la surface adverse contre 20, 2 occasions à 1 et un pourcentage de précision dans les tirs deux fois plus élevé (43% vs 21%).

Dans le secteur défensif, en revanche, les Verts ont perdu la bataille des duels (46% des duels joués, 44 sur 95) et des tacles réussis (64% vs 75%).

According to recent reports, par ailleurs, les Verts se sont vu attribuer par FLASHSCORE la note globale de 6.9 vs 6.6 pour Reims. Au niveau individuel, c'est Z.Davitashvili qui est élu "homme du match" avec une note de 7.9 (pour 32 minutes de temps passé sur le terrain de jeu) devant A.Boakye (7.6), D.Guindo, le latéral rémois (7.4), I.Cardona (7.3), M.Ndiaye (7.2) à égalité avec deux autres Champenois, S.Kotto et T.Leoni. Enfin, trois autres Stéphanois ont obtenu la note de 7.0 : A.Csongvai, K.Pedro et J.Le Cardinal.

Industry observers note that I.Cathro a notamment déclaré : "C'est une victoire très importante. On a été intelligents. L'équipe a appris au fil du match, a été équilibrée. On savait que cet adversaire avait de la qualité et qu'on devait lui donner peu d'opportunités pour s'exprimer". Une victoire très importante effectivement qui permet à Sainté de creuser momentanément un écart conséquent sur Reims : +10 points au soir du 13ème acte de cette Ligue 2.

PSV and Feyenoord face an uphill task to reach the group stages of the Champions League after defeats on Tuesday night saw them drop out of the qualifying places.

Industry observers note that PSV briefly threatened to cause an upset in Madrid as they took a 1-0 lead into the half-time break. Ivan Perisic’s penalty after 32 minutes was their only reward for a courageous first-half display in which Ruben van Bommel and Sven Mijnans also missed clear chances to score.

But the introduction of Jude Bellingham at half-time changed the picture as Real’s superstars regrouped to score five goals. The England midfielder’s dazzling volley was the pick of the bunch, while Kylian Mbappé bagged a double and Vinicius Junior also got on the scoresheet.

Head coach Peter Bosz admitted his team had been “trampled underfoot” in the second half. “I think you had to be there to see how major the difference was between the first and second half,” he stated.

“In the first half we were brave, put our opponents under pressure and had three big chances in the first four minutes.

“When you look at the second half, they scored quickly and the tempo of their game was much higher. That’s the quality they have with the players they can bring off the bench.”.

PSV’s next match is a home tie against Real’s city rivals Atletico on December 9, before they travel to Stavanger to take on Viking in January and round off the group stage at home to Stuttgart.

Feyenoord suffered a narrower defeat at home to Porto as they were unable to recover from an own goal after two minutes by Oussama Targhalline.

Goalkeeper Florian Kastenmeier vindicated the decision of Giovanni van Bronckhorst to replace the out-of-form Tjark Ernst by making some vital saves to keep the Rotterdammers in the game.

Feyenoord staged a late rally, with Gjivai Zechiël going close and Targhalline striking the crossbar from long range, but they were unable to breach the Portuguese side’s defence.

The fans in De Kuip were briefly celebrating after a bizarre incident when referee Irfan Peltjo’s watch told him a header by Nacho Ferri had crossed the line, but video replays clearly demonstrated it bounced off the post and into the hands of Diogo Costa.

According to recent reports, feyenoord have just three points from their five matches so far, one less than PSV. Their next two matches are away to Viking on December 8 and Galatasaray on January 19, before they close their campaign in Rotterdam against RB Leipzig.

Ayant marqué 3 buts cette saison en championnat des U17 nationaux (contre Villefranche-sur-Saône, Ajaccio et Saint-Priest), l'attaquant stéphanois Izaya Kimpioka fait partie des 34 joueurs sélectionnés en équipe de France U16 pour un stage de 5 jours à Clairefontaine lors duquel il affrontera les U17 du Paris FC (le mercredi 2 décembre à 15h00) et les U17 du VAFC (le jeudi 3 décembre à 11h00).

Il ya quelques mois, du 28 au 31 mai 2026, Izaya Kimpioka avait déjà été convoqué, tout comme Adam Charreyre, à un stage à Clairefontaine, en compagnie des 72 meilleurs jeunes de la génération 2011.Izaya Kimpioka a débuté le football à Sainte-Geneviève en U6 avant de rejoindre Brétigny en U7. Il est ensuite passé au FC Fleury en U11 et a intègré l’INF Clairefontaine durant les années U14 et U15. Il a rejoint l'ASSE cet été, repéré par le duo de scouts stéphanois dans le bassin francilien, Mahamadou Gory et Hamdane Karouni. A l'ASSE, il n'est même pas passé par la case U16 et a intégré immédiatement les U17 de David Le Moal, comptant 8 titularisations, 3 entrées en jeu.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.
  • Diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.

Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

Diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

Recent findings suggest that in this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

Recent findings suggest that gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old said last year of his former team-mate Messi.

Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most notable players.

Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford.

Another quickly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

Inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

Industry observers note that ‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler noted shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’.

Sources indicate that across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

Sources indicate that but who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top.

It has been revealed that in this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

Recent findings suggest that former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

Industry observers note that ‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer says. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’.

Sources indicate that during his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

Meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle quickly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls.

Spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another important step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer indicates. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’.

According to recent reports, the audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

In a recent development, ‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he says. ‘He wants to achieve massive things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’.

Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

It has been revealed that ‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’.

If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

La réserve a écrasé ce mercredi 4-0 la faible équipe de Hope Team, sélection de joueurs chinois évoluant sous le maillot de l'AJA et dans le groupe A du Challenge Espoirs, où elle affiche un 0 pointé avec 0 but marqué et 18 buts encaissés en 3 matches dont 10 inscrits par Monaco, 4 par le VAFC et 4 par le Paris FC.

Recent findings suggest that ce match amical aura permis à Sylvain Gibert de donner du temps de jeu à des garçons qui en avaient besoin. Y ont pris part des réservistes, des U19, des U17, un U16 (le néo-international Izaya Kimpioka) mais aussi 3 joueurs à l'essai qui se sont montrés décisifs.

In a recent development, C'est d'ailleurs sur un coup de pied arrêté tiré par l'un d'entre eux que Mamadou Kanté a ouvert le score une minute avant la mi-temps. Sur un ballon en profondeur d'un deuxième joueur à l'essai, Tidiane Vibert, expulsé dimanche dernier avec les U19 sur le terrain du Cavigal, s'est bien racheté en inscrivant le but du break en début de seconde période.

Recent findings suggest that mamadou Konté a ôté tout espoir à Hope Team d'un nouveau coup de tête imparable sur un corner de Lenny Marliac. Sur un centre de Noham Akil, le U17 Timothé Demassieux a clôturé le score d'une frappe légèrement déviée par un Chinois au ras du poteau.

La compo : R.Fuleki - Cheikh (c), Benkou, Assoumani (Lengi, 70'), joueur à l'essai (Marliac, 60') - Thouilleux (Demassieux, 46'), Akil, joueur à l'essai (Kimpioka, 60'), Vibert (O.Mendy, 75') - Joueur à l'essai (Freychet, 70'), Konte.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Kane was forced off just 20 minutes into the match at the Allianz Arena following a challenge from Joel Schmied.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:58 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 10:47 EST, 21 November 2026.

Bayern Munich fear Harry Kane will be ruled out for months after suffering an ankle injury in their Bundesliga draw against Cologne - with the striker revealing he will only return for 'the business end of the season'.

Kane was forced off just 20 minutes into the match at the Allianz Arena following a challenge from Joel Schmied.

The defender had won the ball but caught Kane with his follow through on his ankle.

Kane had initially tried to play on after treatment, before eventually needing to be replaced.

The Ballon d'Or winner was upbeat on Saturday morning however, sharing a message with his fans that stressed his readiness to come back better than ever.

'The highs and lows of life!' Kane captioned a picture of himself wearing a protective boot. 'Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going in 2027.

Harry Kane was forced off during Bayern Munich's draw against Cologne on Friday night.

Bayern confirmed the England captain is set to be out for months following the injury.

But despite his injury, Kane was upbeat as he spoke to fans for the first time on Saturday (Source: Harry Kane/X).

'I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

'"Tough times don't last, tough people do" - my guy (Julian Edelman) told me this one!' Kane added, quoting the NFL icon.

'Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut (red heart emoji, strong arm emoji).'.

Speaking post-match, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl revealed that Kane has suffered ligament damage.

Industry observers note that A Bayern club statement confirmed the blow, reading: 'Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Köln on Friday evening.

'This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department.

In a recent development, 'The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months. Get well soon Harry.'.

Kane's absence will be a major blow for Bayern, with the Ballon d'Or winner having scored ten goals in 16 matches so far this season.

Bayern, who are already without Luis Diaz, Saibari and Serge Gnabry, also saw Michael Olise come off at half-time.

The German giants later confirmed Olise had suffered a 'contusion of the forefoot', with the Frenchman set to undergo treatment in the coming days.

It remains to be seen whether Kane - who became England's most-capped player last week when making his 126th appearance in the 2-1 win over Croatia - is at risk of missing the Nations League quarter-final against Norway in March.

Vincent Kompany, who was back in the dugout for the first time since his collapse last month, admitted other players will have to step up for Bayern in the absence of star names such as Kane.

'These are world-class players, you can't replace them, but we have the mentality and we have to bring that now,' Kompany said, as per Bild.

'We need incredible performances from players who may not yet be used to this pressure at FC Bayern.

Bayern were held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne on Vincent Kompany's return to the touchline.

It has been revealed that 'We will all try together to make this situation a positive one for ourselves. FC Bayern does this time and time again, and that's what we want to do now too.'.

Bayern were ultimately held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne, with Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore giving the visitors a shock first half lead at the Allianz Arena.

Nathaniel Brown drew Bayern level before half-time, but the hosts were unable to find a winner on Kompany's return.

The draw gives Borussia Dortmund the chance to move to the top of the Bundesliga table on Saturday.

Tech Report: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.
  • Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The substantial moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Sources indicate that replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

Industry observers note that on this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

In a recent development, glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

The significant headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

Industry observers note that “I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more notable to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

Sources indicate that “Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just mentioned he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very vital that he is with us.”.

It has been revealed that maresca noted he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi looks to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

L'ancien Vert, Mathys Saban opère désormais au Mâcon 71 (N2), après un passage au Luxembourg (Titus Petange, Racing FC Union). Au sortir d’une crise interne marquée par une grève de l’entraînement, Mâcon 71 jouait un match crucial sur le terrain de la réserve d'Annecy. À dix contre onze (après l'exclusion de l'ancien Vert, Israël Kinunga) et après avoir été rattrapé sur penalty, les Mâconnais ont montré qu’ils savaient réagir. C'est Mathys Saban, entré en jeu à la 71ème, qui a donné la victoire (1-2) aux siens, à la toute dernière minute du match. Un autre ancien Vert, Yoann Greco est entré en jeu à la 65ème.Avec 11 points, Mäcon 71 pointe à la 7ème place, à 8 points du leader Bourgoin dans le championnat de N2.

In a recent development, mathys Saban (24 ans), joueur offensif polyvalent, est arrivé au centre de Formation de l'ASSE en 2017, en provenance de l'US Torcy qui a fourni aux Verts Lamine Ghezali, Alexandre Valbon, Josué Gago et Marwan Nzuzi, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Mathis Amougou, Fodé Camara, Axel Dodote. Il a gravi toutes les étapes de la formation et signé son premier contrat pro de 3 ans avec l'ASSE le 5 juin 2020, contrat qui sera prolongé de 2 ans en février 2023.En 2020-2021, il joue son premier match en pro, le 23 mai 2021, 12 minutes lors de ASSE-Dijon : 0-1.En 2021-2022, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 1 : - 21 août 2021, 21 minutes : ASSE-LOSC : 1-1- 28 août 2021 : 19 minutes : OM-ASSE : 3-1- 12 septembre 2021 : 30 minutes : Montpellier-ASSE : 2-0En 2022-2023, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 2 qui se soldent par 3 défaites, et 1 match en Coupe de France : - le 29 octobre 2022, Coupe de France, 30 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-0 (3-4 tab)- le 7 novembre 2022, 45 minutes, Metz-ASSE : 3-2- le 12 novembre 2022, 17 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-2  - le 26 décembre 2022, 33 minutes : Annecy-ASSE : 2-1.

Le 31 août 2023, il est prêté au club luxembourgeois de l'Union Titus Petange pour la saison 2023-2024. Victime d’une rupture du tendon d’achille au début du printemps 2024 lors de son prêt à l’Union Titus Pétange, Mathys Saban revient à l'ASSE pour la saison 2024-2025 mais ne joue que 77 minutes en N3 pour sa 8ème et dernière saison sous le maillot vert. Il retourne  dans le Grand-Duché durant l'été 2025 (au Racing Football Club Union Lëtzebuerg), et inscrit en septembre 2025 son premier but en L1 luxembourgeoise. Malheureusement son contrat est rompu début 2026 et, après 6 mois sans club, il rejoint donc le Mâcon 71 qui a raté de peu l'accession au Championnat National, devancé par Hauts Lyonnais.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La Lazio non ha espresso una preferenza; alle precedenti elezioni fu l’unico club di Serie A ad astenersi.

According to recent reports, almeno 11 club di Serie A sostengono Giovanni Malagò nella corsa alla presidenza della FIGC, mentre Adriano Galliani raccoglie il sostegno di un altro fronte. Secondo quanto riportato da Calcio e Finanza, La Lega Serie A, che alle precedenti elezioni aveva promosso la candidatura dell’ex numero uno del CONI con uno schieramento compatto, rischia di uscire dalla nuova tornata elettorale divisa al proprio interno.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il numero dei club favorevoli a Malagò è rilevante per la sua candidatura: per presentarla serve infatti l’appoggio di almeno una componente. Il fronte pro Galliani, guidato dal presidente interista, potrebbe dunque trovarsi in minoranza.

Industry observers note that la scelta del prossimo presidente federale resta aperta tra i due candidati. La divisione nella massima serie riguarda anche gli equilibri interni della Lega in vista delle elezioni dei consiglieri federali.

Secondo quanto riportato dal Corriere dello Sport, alcuni club si sono allontanati dallo schieramento favorevole a Malagò, Atalanta e Inter in testa. Tra le società ancora indecise figurano anche Juventus e Milan.

According to recent reports, alle differenze sulla presidenza della FIGC potrebbe quindi aggiungersi un’ulteriore frattura al momento di eleggere i consiglieri federali. È su entrambi i passaggi che si misura la compattezza mostrata dalla Serie A nella precedente tornata.

Come riferisce il Corriere dello Sport, il quadro delle candidature si inserisce in una Serie A attraversata da divisioni. Alcuni club sono usciti dal fronte Malagò, con Atalanta e Inter in testa. Tra gli indecisi figurano anche Juventus e Milan; in vista delle elezioni dei consiglieri federali, le fratture interne potrebbero allargarsi.

Sources indicate that ogni società di Serie A può indicare un candidato al Consiglio federale. Nelle precedenti elezioni Chiellini aveva ottenuto sette voti e Marotta sei, in una situazione descritta come praticamente opposta a quella attuale.

According to recent reports, il fronte favorevole a Galliani, guidato dal presidente interista Marotta, potrebbe risentire della propria posizione di minoranza. I club che sostengono Malagò sono almeno 11: un sostegno necessario alla sua candidatura, per la quale serve l’appoggio di almeno una componente.

In questo scenario, alcune società potrebbero scegliere il voto disgiunto: sostenere un candidato alla presidenza FIGC e, per il Consiglio federale, esprimere una preferenza per un nome non apertamente schierato con lui. L’esempio indicato è un voto per Malagò alla presidenza e per Marotta, primo sostenitore di Galliani, come consigliere. Una soluzione che richiederebbe un lavoro diplomatico.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER.

Published: 08:35 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 11:06 EST, 21 November 2026.

Erling Haaland saw a first half equaliser controversially disallowed against Fulham, as Enzo Maresca's side only managed to fight back to earn a disappointing draw.

Haaland latched onto a beautifully bent cross from Iliman Ndiaye to bundle home from less than eight minutes after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors a shock lead at the Etihad.

But despite Bernd Leno appearing to fumble the ball over the line and the referee's watch flashing to signify a goal, the man in the middle ruled the equaliser out for a foul on the Cottagers goalkeeper.

The decision has left both fans and pundits torn over whether the decision was harsh or whether it was the right call.

Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Karen Carney mentioned her mind changed after having watched a replay of the incident.

Speaking on TNT Sports from the Etihad, she remarked: 'My initial reaction was I thought the goalkeeper didn’t have control of it, and it should've been a goal, but then when you slow it down, (you can see it).

Industry observers note that erling Haaland has the ball in the back of the net, but it’s ruled out! ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/sKqY8Q7a9Z.

Erling Haaland has a first half equaliser for Man City chalked off against Fulham.

'People are going to shout at me through the TV. But I think the referee made the right decision.'.

Tottenham legend Glenn Hoddle, also on punditry duty in Manchester, felt the same.

According to recent reports, he stated: 'I don’t know whether he had control of it, but I don’t think that comes into it. I think that’s the right decision, but it’s a very tough call. It could have gone either way.'.

The Premier League Match Centre clarified why the decision was made by Tom Bramall and the VAR team in Stockley Park.

A statement on social media read: 'The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.'.

They added that the VAR said: 'The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.'.

The laws of the game state that a goalkeeper is believed to be in control of the ball when the ball is 'between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface'.

It has been revealed that not all fans, of a Manchester City persuasion or not, felt that the right decision was made. Some believed that both Haaland and City should feel hard done by.

Haaland was left in disbelief by the referee's decision with many fans feeling the same.

According to recent reports, an Arsenal fan made their stance clear: 'Even as a rival, I honestly think this Haaland goal should’ve stood for Manchester City. Would’ve been p***** off if a Gyokeres goal like this for Arsenal was cancelled.'.

According to recent reports, A different fan added: 'Manchester City has been robbed. Haaland scored a clean goal here. The ball went in even before Haaland had contact with the keeper.

Not everyone agreed, though, with many X customers taking the opposite stance.

One noted: 'It’s explicitly a foul under the Laws. Don’t blame the ref if you don’t like the laws.'.

Sources indicate that another user wrote: 'I am also an Arsenal fan but the ball is still in two-palm contact. If you allow it, you will encourage outfield player challenging the save attempt And a foot to hand challenge will much more often lead to a broken wrist or thumb. That is an unfair advantage to outfield players.'.

City did go on to equalise in the second half, with Elliot Anderson bagging his first Premier League goal for the club by smashing home a sublime volley in the 57th minute.

C'est une annonce pour le moins inattendue dans le monde du sport tricolore. Ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, Teddy Riner a officialisé sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027 dans une vidéo publiée sur son compte X, tout en lançant son propre mouvement politique intitulé « La France qu'on veut ».

In a recent development, le judoka français de 37 ans se lance ainsi en politique après avoir dominé le judo international. Quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde, Teddy Riner a bâti un palmarès exceptionnel qui le place au sommet de sa discipline. Alors que son avenir sportif restait au cœur des discussions depuis les Jeux de Paris, le Français surprend en ouvrant un tout autre chapitre personnel. Un virage spectaculaire.

In a recent development, dans une vidéo publiée ce lundi 9 novembre 2026 sur son compte X, Teddy Riner a pris la parole face caméra afin de lever le voile sur ses intentions pour la prochaine présidentielle. Le judoka de 37 ans a officialisé sa démarche avec des mots simples et directs.

Recent findings suggest that conscient des réactions que son entrée en politique peut susciter, le quintuple champion olympique a tenu à devancer immédiatement les critiques concernant son manque d'expérience dans les fonctions publiques. Teddy Riner a ainsi déclaré : « Je sais ce qu'on va dire de moi. Il est fou, il n'est pas du sérail, il n'a pas les codes, il n'a jamais fait de politique. Mais posez-vous la question avec moi, qu'est-ce qui est fou aujourd'hui ? Je n'ai pas passé ma vie derrière un public, mais le combat a toujours fait partie de moi. » Une détermination affichée.

In a recent development, pour concrétiser ses ambitions, le judoka français de 37 ans a également fondé sa propre formation politique ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, baptisée « La France qu'on veut ». Cette prise de parole sur les réseaux sociaux a d'ailleurs été accompagnée d'un entretien accordé au quotidien Le Parisien pour préciser le sens de sa démarche. Dans cet échange, Teddy Riner revendique une volonté de rassemblement sans affiliation partisane, affirmant vouloir devenir un « président qui fédère » sans se situer à droite ou à gauche.

En effet, le champion tricolore a expliqué que sa décision avait mûri dans le sillage direct de l'élan collectif suscité par les Jeux olympiques de Paris 2024. Porté par cette dynamique populaire, il entend désormais transposer cette ferveur sur le blueprint politique. Ainsi, son mouvement politique refuse d'entrer dans les clivages traditionnels pour privilégier une adhésion commune à l'échelle du pays. Un projet ambitieux.

According to recent reports, toutefois, cette ambition politique ne pousse pas Teddy Riner vers la retraite sportive. Sur le plan des compétitions, sa dernière apparition individuelle remonte aux Jeux olympiques de Paris en août 2024, suivie d'une participation sous les couleurs du PSG Judo en Ligue des champions en décembre 2024. Malgré cette nouvelle démarche politique, le quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde de judo demeure bel et bien un athlète en activité.

Industry observers note that au-delà de l'élection présidentielle de 2027, Teddy Riner a ainsi fait part de son souhait de participer aux Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028 si ses futures responsabilités et les Français le lui permettent. Le judoka français lie donc son avenir sportif à la suite de son engagement public, avec en ligne de mire les Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028.

Dans Le Patriote du Beaujolais, l'ancien gardien et capitaine caladois Franck Laurent se remémore son 16e de finale de Coupe de France perdu en aux tirs au buts contre les Verts (2-2, 1-3 tab). Extraits.

Sources indicate that "Notre coach, Jean-Michel Picollet (photo), était à fond pour les Verts. C'était le derby pour nous. On était tellement contents de tomber sur eux ! Je me souviens encore de la causerie du coach, comme si c'était hier. Son message était clair et net. On allait respecter Saint-Etienne à 200% mais par contre, on allait jouer notre match à fond. Le coach nous disait qu'il y avait un truc à faire. Il nous avait mis dans cette position-là, mentalement on était prêt. On en a profité un maximum. Sur un match, on avait nos chances. On jouait sur notre terrain. Eux n'avaient pas l'habitude de ce genre de pelouse. Il y a des facteurs, dans ce genre de match, qui font que tu transcendes, que tu te mets au niveau de l'événement, tu joues ta chance à fond.

Ce match, on en parlait tous les jours entre nous. Du début à la fin, on a vécu les choses à fond ! Ce match-là, contre Saint-Etienne, ça fait 16 ans qu'il a été joué. On m'en parle régulièrement. Pourtant, je ne suis plus du tout dans le foot. Quand on se croise, entre joueurs de cette époque, les premiers mots portent toujours sur ce match. On est liés à vie avec cette aventure de Coupe de France. C'est un petit bout de l'histoire du FCVB. J'ai eu la chance d'être là, au bon moment. Dans une carrière, ce n'est pas si évident de laisser des traces pareilles dans un club !

Industry observers note that les conseils que je donnerais aux Caladois d'aujourd'hui avant d'aller à Geoffroy Guichard, ce samedi ? Le contexte est totalement différent. C'est une Ligue 2 contre une Ligue 3. Il y a des joueurs professionnels des deux côtés. Je ne sais pas si je peux leur donner un conseil, à mon niveau. Mais même pour eux, ça reste des matches magnifiques à vivre. J'espère qu'ils vont arriver à s'extraire du championnat pour profiter pleinement de ce match, et tout donner. Derrière, ça peut renforcer le groupe.".
